review_cadence: quarterly; best practice for agentic engineering changes within months
method: AEMS method: see README (Method, Scoring method, Sources)

rules.move: Add verification capacity before adding agent throughput: wire tests, lint and type checks into the agent loop (hooks) and run them in CI on every PR.
rules.rationale: Agent change volume already exceeds what tests and CI gates cover. Review is the binding constraint; more agents only lengthen the queue.
rules.source: Faros AI (PR review time +91%, PR size +154%); Chen & Stratton 2026 (review is the bottleneck); NBER w35275 weak-link (commits +240% -> releases +30%)
rules.expected_effect: Verification-debt ratio falls toward <= 1; review time stabilises.
rules.not_yet: Do not add parallel agents or background loops until the ratio is <= 1.

rules.move: Make the gates observable: CI on every PR with results retained, and track pass rate plus failing-gate -> self-correction cycles.
rules.rationale: Sensor configs are present but there is no evidence they run and block. Presence of artefacts without outcome movement is maturity theatre.
rules.source: AEMS outcome cap (README, Scoring method); Thoughtworks Technology Radar Apr 2026 (feedback sensors, harness engineering)
rules.expected_effect: Lifts the level-2 cap once run history shows gates executing and passing.
rules.not_yet: Do not add more sensor tools until the existing ones are proven to run.

rules.move: Establish a one-command test run and CI that executes it; add a pre-commit or agent hook so failures reach the agent before a human does.
rules.rationale: Agents that validate succeed more often; validation needs a deterministic gate the agent can call.
rules.source: TraceProbe / 'Beyond resolution rates' (validation effort rho=+0.50 with success); Thoughtworks Radar Apr 2026 (feedback sensors)
rules.expected_effect: First-pass acceptance up, fewer human review rounds on mechanical defects.
rules.not_yet: Mutation testing and fitness functions can wait until the basic gate is reliable.

rules.move: Add fitness sensors for agent-typical decay: mutation testing on agent-written tests, duplication/complexity budgets, architecture rules.
rules.rationale: AI-era code shows more duplication and complexity that ordinary tests do not catch.
rules.source: GitClear 2026 (duplication +81%, refactoring -70%); 'AI IDEs or Autonomous Agents?' 2026 (static-analysis warnings +18%, cognitive complexity +39%)
rules.expected_effect: Maintainability delta stays at or below repo baseline.
rules.not_yet: Do not gate on coverage percentage alone.

rules.move: Fix or delete stale references in instruction files, then ablate: remove rules one at a time and keep only those whose removal hurts.
rules.rationale: Instruction files that point at missing paths mislead agents; agents follow context files, so unnecessary or wrong rules make tasks harder.
rules.source: 'Evaluating AGENTS.md' arXiv 2602.11988 (context files reduce success in 5/8 settings, cost +20-23%); 'Agent READMEs' arXiv 2511.12884 (files evolve like config code)
rules.expected_effect: Lower agent cost per task; fewer wrong-file edits.
rules.not_yet: Do not add new rules until stale ones are gone.

rules.move: Add one minimal root instruction file (AGENTS.md): build and test commands, boundaries, how to verify. Keep it short.
rules.rationale: A sanctioned, minimal context file is the entry point; long files measurably hurt.
rules.source: 'Evaluating AGENTS.md' arXiv 2602.11988 (keep minimal); 'Agent READMEs' arXiv 2511.12884 (76% cover tests)
rules.expected_effect: Fewer clarification turns; consistent commands across agents.
rules.not_yet: Do not import a generic template or long style guide.

rules.move: Move path-specific rules into scoped files (progressive disclosure) and add the missing security and performance guardrails.
rules.rationale: Root files grow by accretion; scoped rules keep each agent's context minimal. Security and performance are the least-covered topics.
rules.source: 'Agent READMEs' arXiv 2511.12884 (security 15%, performance 15%); 'Evaluating AGENTS.md' arXiv 2602.11988
rules.expected_effect: Smaller per-task context; fewer security findings at review.
rules.not_yet: Do not add rules without a failure that motivated them.

rules.move: Close the loop: when the same mistake happens twice, change the instruction file in the same fix commit and reference the incident.
rules.rationale: Level 5 needs instruction diffs traceable to incidents, not periodic rewrites.
rules.source: AEMS dim 7 and level 5 (README, Method); 'Programming by Chat' ASE 2026, arXiv 2604.00436 (plans externalised into persistent artefacts)
rules.expected_effect: Recurring corrections (S2) fall.
rules.not_yet: Do not auto-append every lesson; dedupe and decay.

rules.move: Externalise plans: one short plan or spec file per non-trivial change, checked in next to the code.
rules.rationale: Programming with agents is progressive specification; persistent plans let a fresh agent gather context before editing.
rules.source: 'Programming by Chat' ASE 2026, arXiv 2604.00436 (progressive specification, externalised plans); TraceProbe (context before editing rho=+0.68)
rules.expected_effect: Fewer front-loaded patches; shorter correction loops.
rules.not_yet: Do not mandate heavyweight PRDs for small fixes.

rules.move: Adopt a spec-driven flow for feature work (proposal -> spec -> tasks -> apply -> archive) and record decisions with reasons as ADRs.
rules.rationale: Spec artefacts per change are the level-3 signature; decisions with reasons are what later agents need.
rules.source: GitHub Spec-Kit; OpenSpec; PRDBench arXiv 2510.24358
rules.expected_effect: Share of feature commits with a spec rises; clarification rounds and rework from unclear intent fall.
rules.not_yet: Do not let specs grow unbounded; long context hurts.

rules.move: Make specs replayable: grade acceptance criteria as binary MET/UNMET checks with file:line evidence by a fresh agent.
rules.rationale: Binary decomposition lifts grader agreement to human level and tests whether a stranger could build from the spec.
rules.source: PRDBench arXiv 2510.24358 (replayable PRD-based evaluation)
rules.expected_effect: Measured spec replayability; better first-pass acceptance.
rules.not_yet: Do not score spec length.

rules.move: Route agent changes through PRs with a named human review line and keep batches small.
rules.rationale: Direct-to-main agent changes bypass the only gate that catches high-severity issues; large agent PRs swamp reviewers.
rules.source: DORA 2025 AI Capabilities (small batches); Faros AI (PR size +154%, review time +91%)
rules.expected_effect: Agent-gated share up; median PR size down.
rules.not_yet: Do not enable unattended merge modes.

rules.move: Risk-tier the review line and earn autonomy with evidence: explicit per-project modes (local-only / direct-PR / full-gate), branch protection, and watch for reviewer habituation.
rules.rationale: Approvals of agent PRs drift up while inline comments fall; autonomy should be earned per step, not assumed.
rules.source: GitLab AI maturity ladder (earn autonomy with evidence); 'Habituation at the Gate' arXiv 2606.22721 (approval +14.5pp, inline comments -22%)
rules.expected_effect: Stable review depth as volume grows.
rules.not_yet: Do not grant +yolo modes on high-blast-radius paths.

rules.move: Ignore .env* in git, remove any tracked secret-like files, and add secret scanning to pre-commit and CI.
rules.rationale: Agents copy what is in reach; transcripts and commits leak secrets that are not fenced off.
rules.source: SWE-chat arXiv 2604.20779 (agent code has more security vulnerabilities per line)
rules.expected_effect: Zero tracked secret-like files; zero pattern hits.
rules.not_yet: Do not grant agents broader tool permissions first.

rules.move: Declare agent permissions in the repo: allow/deny lists in agent settings, reviewed MCP server configs, CODEOWNERS on sensitive paths.
rules.rationale: Tool permissions and ownership are the blast-radius controls the dimension requires.
rules.source: AEMS dim 8 (README, Method); 'Agent READMEs' arXiv 2511.12884 (security covered in only 15% of files)
rules.expected_effect: Auditable tool scope per repo.
rules.not_yet: Do not add MCP servers without an allow-list.

rules.move: Add receipts: AI-share attribution with coverage on every PR, and per-task cost budgets.
rules.rationale: Attribution without coverage misleads; budgets turn cost into a reviewable signal.
rules.source: AEMS dim 8 (README, Method); repowise attribution practice (report coverage, withhold shares below 30% coverage)
rules.expected_effect: Audit trail per change; cost per surviving unit becomes computable.
rules.not_yet: Do not publish AI-share numbers with unknown coverage.

rules.move: Turn on attribution: a Co-authored-by trailer (or bot author) on every agent commit, and conventional commit types so fixes are classifiable.
rules.rationale: Without attribution, AI-share, rework and survival cannot be measured, and self-reports are unreliable.
rules.source: METR RCT Jul 2025 (believed -20%, measured +19% slower); Stanford SEP (rework 2.6x); attribution from trailers and bot authors (README, Attribution)
rules.expected_effect: Attributed AI-share becomes a measured number instead of a guess.
rules.not_yet: Do not report productivity uplift from surveys.

rules.move: Track collaboration-quality metrics on a cadence: first-pass acceptance, post-merge rework at 30/90 days, review burden.
rules.rationale: Output counts measure the model; first-pass and rework measure whether the human-agent system works.
rules.source: Thoughtworks Technology Radar Apr 2026 (measuring collaboration quality); Stanford SEP (rework 2.6x); Faros AI (review +91%)
rules.expected_effect: Rework visible per month; drives the outcome checks in other dims.
rules.not_yet: Do not rank individuals on these numbers.

rules.move: Join outcomes at 90 days: survival and usage of agent-written lines, by task class.
rules.rationale: Task-level gains shrink at release and usage; survival is the anchor metric.
rules.source: SWE-chat arXiv 2604.20779 (~59% of agent code survives to commit); NBER w35275 (commits +240% -> releases +30%)
rules.expected_effect: Usage-weighted output replaces commit counts.
rules.not_yet: Do not treat deleted code as waste without usage data.

rules.move: Prove the practice works before adding more artefacts: measure matured rework and first-pass acceptance for agent changes.
rules.rationale: The artefacts for a higher level exist, but there is no outcome evidence that they help. Presence is not maturity.
rules.source: AEMS outcome cap (README, Scoring method: presence is not maturity); 'Evaluating AGENTS.md' arXiv 2602.11988 (presence != benefit)
rules.expected_effect: Lifts the level-2 cap once >= 5 matured agent commits show healthy rework.
rules.not_yet: Do not add more files to pass a checklist.
